newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen denies release of Polish hostages.
newsitem.headline: Yemen denies release of Polish hostages.

text.p: A Yemeni official denied on Tuesday a report that five Polish tourists abducted by Yemeni tribesmen last week had been released.
"Negotiations are still underway, the government is not sparing any efforts to end the situation, and we hope for a solution soon," the official told Reuters.
A Polish foreign ministry report had earlier said that the tribesmen freed the hostages.
But a Polish embassy official in Sanaa later said the release had not been confirmed.

The tourists -- three men and two women between the ages of 50 and 64 -- were kidnapped on their way to archaeological sites in eastern Yemen last week. It was the second abduction of European holidaymakers in December.

The tourists were abducted by members of the al-Masni tribe in the Khawlan area, about 65 km (40 miles) east of the capital Sanaa. Diplomats said the abduction took place sometime between Tuesday and Thursday.
